title: Episode 69 — Bobby Lee and Bill Poon
summary: Bill Poon is introduced through his work driving and scheduling for adult workers, then Bobby Lee joins for an unusually long conversation that ranges across Asian-American representation, comedy, recovery, childhood drug use and sexual behavior, domestic violence, family loyalty, pornography, sex work, friendship, racism, and consent. The most consequential material is not trivia: the episode repeatedly turns hesitation, surprise genital touching, visible performer distress, and persistence after refusal into entertainment or technique. The editorial map preserves those statements as historical evidence while directly rejecting them as guidance. It also preserves Bobby Lee's first-person recovery and family testimony without turning relatives, former partners, workers, clients, or a young audience participant into searchable dossiers.
sensitivity: Childhood sexual behavior and intoxication; early methamphetamine use and rehabilitation; domestic and sibling violence; addiction and relapse; suicidal language immediately disclaimed; explicit sexual content; pornography and performer distress; surprise genital touching, escalation after hesitation, rape jokes, and sexual harassment; adult work and private client logistics; private partners and young audience participant; HIV and anatomy misinformation; racial, gender, sexuality, disability, body, age, and suicide stereotypes; genital cosmetic surgery pressure.
speaker_policy: Named dialogue remains withheld. Episode 69 has zero diarized turns and five coarse window embeddings for a multi-person episode. Context identifies public guests, but no independently held-out multispeaker test has passed and no name is inferred from transcript content.

source_notes.claim: Consent is voluntary, informed, specific, reversible, and must be present for each act; silence, hesitation, intoxication, and a prior yes are not permission
source_notes.use: corrects surprise touching, escalation after hesitation, bodily-contact penalties, and performer-distress passages

source_notes.claim: Methamphetamine is highly addictive and can produce cardiovascular, neurological, dental, psychiatric, and overdose harms
source_notes.use: rejects methamphetamine as childhood comedy or weight-loss advice

source_notes.claim: HIV can affect anyone with relevant exposure; condoms, PrEP, PEP, sterile injection equipment, testing, and effective treatment are prevention tools
source_notes.use: corrects the claim that Koreans cannot acquire HIV

source_notes.claim: Most condoms are highly effective against HIV and some other STIs when used correctly; lubricant reduces tearing risk
source_notes.use: corrects condomless-sex and anal-sex risk discussion

source_notes.claim: The hymen is not proof of virginity and virginity is not determined by hymenal appearance
source_notes.use: corrects 'legally still virgin' and hymen claims

source_notes.claim: Female genital appearance varies normally; cosmetic genital surgery can carry pain, scarring, altered sensation, and other risks and should not be driven by pressure
source_notes.use: corrects labial stereotypes and surgery pressure

source_notes.claim: Recovery is personal and may include clinical care, medication, peer and family support, faith, and self-care
source_notes.use: frames Bobby Lee's recovery testimony without prescribing one pathway

source_notes.claim: Child sexual behavior must be evaluated developmentally and in context; coercion, age or power differences, distress, and impairment are important warning signs
source_notes.use: prevents adult sexual banter from becoming the framing for the childhood account
